Resonance user documentation

One shared file tree. A private folder for every member.

Work in Resonance or with local tools. Verified file bytes synchronize between authorized peers, and unsafe concurrent changes stay visible until someone resolves them.

02 · How it works

Your folder reflects the shared workspace

Keys, databases, operation history, and private blob storage stay outside the folder.

  1. 01

    Choose

    Bind a new or empty folder outside Git management. A new workspace begins with plans.

  2. 02

    Work

    Edit rendered Markdown in Resonance or change ordinary files with local applications.

  3. 03

    Synchronize

    Resonance exchanges signed file history and verifies binary content when authorized peers connect.

  4. 04

    Resolve

    Safe Markdown changes merge. Competing edits, deletions, creations, and moves remain available for review.

03 · What ships

The current workspace file experience

The first release favors recoverable file history over silent conflict resolution.

File tree
Nested folders and ordinary files
Markdown
Rendered editing and local tools
Binary data
Verified content hashes
Conflicts
Visible, reviewable choices

Recovery

Disconnect without losing the record

Work offline, then recover missing operations and file bytes when a peer reconnects.

Private roots

Use a different path on every computer

Members share the logical tree, not absolute paths or local control files.

Root health

Repair, replace, or unbind

Workspace history can continue synchronizing while a local folder is unavailable.
